title: An Afternoon in the Archive
paragraphs: During an afternoon at a community archive, a class examined records of ordinary experiences. Some came from personal journals, while others resembled reports or scenes from fiction. The students agreed that useful evidence could come from a quiet incident as well as a surprising one.

The opening pages introduced several situations worth examining carefully. A narrow stream ran through the quiet dell. A deluge of requests arrived after the announcement. The demagogue used fear instead of evidence to win support. The villain devised a demented plan to control the city.

The remaining pages widened the discussion with additional observations. The agreement required both sides to demilitarize the border zone. The fossil's dentition suggested that the animal ate plants. Heavy logging can denude a hillside of trees. The growing company decided to departmentalize its operations.

The class finished by comparing its first impressions with its later interpretations. Some ideas had survived closer examination; others needed to be revised. The students kept the original details visible so that future readers could judge for themselves. They understood that a convincing explanation should connect the evidence clearly while leaving room for questions the records could not answer.
